overclaims.abstract: These findings provide preliminary quasi-experimental evidence that participation in a multi-component digital literacy and digital wellbeing program is associated with healthier self-reported Internet use, stronger perceived digital competence, and greater delay of gratification.
overclaims.body: Neither the decline in PIU in the wait-list group nor the significant Group × Time interactions can rule out this explanation.
overclaims.why: The body states the significant interactions cannot rule out reporting reactivity as an explanation, so the claim of healthier Internet use and stronger competence is weaker than the abstract implies.

overclaims.abstract: The post-intervention data were statistically consistent with the hypothesized DSE → DGI → PIU indirect pathway; however, alternative-model analyses indicated that DGI showed the more consistent association with PIU across specifications.
overclaims.body: whereas the direct associations of intervention condition and DSEpost with PIUpost were not statistically significant
overclaims.why: The body reports that the direct associations of intervention condition and DSE with PIU were not significant, and that the two single-mediator paths were non-significant, which narrows the pathway support the abstract describes.

unsettled: Significant Group × Time interactions were observed for PIU, DSE, and DGI, indicating more favorable self-reported pre-to-post changes in the intervention group than in the wait-list control group.
